attempted_claim: Is every properly embedded free-boundary minimal annulus Sigma in the closed Euclidean unit 3-ball B^3 with the standard metric, where Sigma is compact of genus zero with exactly two boundary components meeting S^2 orthogonally, admitting exactly one reflection symmetry across a plane through the origin with no second distinct reflection plane assumed and no assumption that the two boundary loops are congruent, necessarily congruent by a rigid motion to the critical catenoid? A complete answer is either a rigorous proof that any such single-plane-symmetric annulus is the critical catenoid, or an explicit counterexample verifying embeddedness, annulus topology, free-boundary minimality, exactly one reflection plane, and a checked geometric invariant proving non-congruence to the critical catenoid.
decisive_failure: Single-mirror symmetry underdetermines the surface: Steklov parity and flux balances each fix at most one component, leaving admissible non-circular symmetric boundary data; no known embedded annulus template exists for a counterexample, and closing either direction needs breakthrough-level rigidity or existence inputs beyond a bounded pass. Worklog and recovery computation are preserved as negative evidence.
